title: Geometric bet sizing
summary: The same share of the pot on every street, so the whole stack is in by the river.

idea.text: **Geometric sizing** is the same share of the pot on every street, chosen so that the last bet puts the whole stack in. A strong hand wins the most this way, and the opponent never gets a cheap street to draw on.

formula.text:
Pot P, effective stack S, streets left to bet N. The share of the pot per street:

**f = ((1 + 2S / P)^(1/N) − 1) / 2**

Check: pot 10, stacks 95, three streets. (1 + 19)^(1/3) ≈ 2.71, so f ≈ 0.86. You bet 86% pot on the flop, turn and river: the pot grows 10 → 27 → 74 → 200, and the river bet is all-in.

table.text:
Reference points for three streets:
- SPR ≈ 4.5 (a 3-bet pot): about 58% pot per street.
- SPR ≈ 9.5 (a normal pot, 100 BB stacks): about 86%.
- SPR ≈ 16: more than the pot every street; without overbets the stack doesn't go in over three streets.

Over two streets (turn and river) at SPR 4.5 you need about 108% pot.

when.text: When geometry fits: you have a strong hand or a polarized range and want the whole stack in by the river. When it doesn't: a medium hand, a merged range, a multiway pot. There pot control matters more.

q-geo.q: Pot 20 BB, stacks 90 BB, three streets ahead. What is the geometric bet?

options: To make bets grow at random
To get the whole stack in by the river with the same share each street
t1.explain: Equal shares of the pot grow it so that the last bet is exactly all-in.

t2.q: With the same number of streets, a bigger SPR means the share per street is…
t2.explain: More stack relative to the pot has to go in over the same streets.

t3.q: Which hand suits geometric sizing best?
options: The nuts or a polarized range
A hand that wants to check-call
t3.explain: Geometry is for hands that want the whole stack in.
